'''Giuseppe Bertin''' (born in [[Adria]], 28 March 1952) is an Italian physicist, known for his work in the explanation of the [[Spiral galaxy|spiral structure of galaxies]], and in the use of these as cosmological probes and [[gravitational lens]]es. Bertin is currently Professor at the [[University of Milan]]. He won the [[Premio Presidente della Repubblica (prize)|Premio Presidente della Repubblica]] in 2013 for his contribute in the latest discoveries in the dynamics of galaxies.

== Biography ==
Bertin obtained a [[Laurea]] in physics, and subsequently a PhD at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]] in [[Pisa]]. Giuseppe Bertin is full professor of [[Astrophysics|Theoretical Astrophysics]] at the [[University of Milan]] and collaborator at the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare|National Institute of Nuclear Physics]]. He is currently considered one of the most influential Italian theoretical astrophysicists on the territory. From '75 to '91 he was first a researcher and then an associate professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mr. Giuseppe Bertin {{!}} ILP|url=https://ilp.mit.edu/node/22972|access-date=2021-10-20|website=ilp.mit.edu}}</ref> He was also a collaborator at the [[Space Telescope Science Institute]] in [[Baltimore]], and at the Kapteyn Astronomical Institute in [[Groningen]]. In the two-year period 2000–2002 he was a member, collaborator and consultant for [[European Southern Observatory|ESO]]'s observation programs. In the three-year period between 2006 and 2009 he became a member of the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=KITP UC Santa Barbara|url=https://www.kitp.ucsb.edu/activities/lens-c06/photos}}</ref>[[University of California, Santa Barbara|, Santa Barbara]]. He is currently a member of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[International Astronomical Union]], the [[American Astronomical Society]], and the [[New York Academy of Sciences|New York Academy Sciences]].

== Research ==
He was a student, researcher and professor at the [[University of Pisa]] and the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale of Pisa]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=ORCID|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6607-3881|access-date=2021-10-20|website=orcid.org}}</ref> He currently holds the role of full professor at the [[Milan school of physics|Physics department]] of the [[University of Milan]], where he teaches theoretical astrophysics. His research focuses on the study of [[globular cluster]]s of galaxies and the [[Galactic disc|disks of galaxies]]. His main scientific results focus more on the explanation of the [[Spiral galaxy|spiral structure]] (normal and barred) of galaxies, and on the use of these as cosmological probes and [[gravitational lens]]es. He also deals with the study of collective phenomena in [[astrophysical plasma]]s and [[Accretion disk|self-gravitating accretion disk]].

== Awards ==
In 2013, he was appointed corresponding member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] thanks to his notable contribution in understanding the dynamics in galaxies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bertin, Giuseppe {{!}} Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei|url=https://www.lincei.it/it/content/bertin-giuseppe|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.lincei.it|language=it}}</ref> In the same year he received the [[Premio Presidente della Repubblica (prize)|President of the Republic Award]] of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]], from the then president [[Giorgio Napolitano]] at the [[Quirinal Palace|Quirinale]] on 24 June.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Portale storico della Presidenza della Repubblica|url=https://archivio.quirinale.it/aspr/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=archivio.quirinale.it|language=it}}</ref> He is the third professor in the Physics department of the University of Milan to receive the award, after [[Giuseppe Occhialini|Beppo Occhialini]] (in '49) and Piero Caldirola (in '56). He also received the [[Lions Clubs International|Lions club]]'s Two Towers Gold Award in 1991.

== Selected publications ==
He is the author of two monographs published by [[MIT Press]] and [[Cambridge University Press]], about 200 refereed articles, and more than 40 invited articles.

* Dynamics of Galaxies (Astronomia), Cambridge University Press; 2ª edizione (21 aprile 2014), {{ISBN|978-1107000544}}.
* Dynamics of Galaxies (Astronomia), Cambridge University Press; 1ª edizione (12 giugno 2000), {{ISBN|978-0521478557}}.
* [https://mitpress.mit.edu/books/spiral-structure-galaxies Spiral Structure in Galaxies (Astronomia): A Density Wave Theory]; Mit Pr; New edizione (1 maggio 1996), {{ISBN|978-0262023962}}
* Collective Phenomena in Macroscopic Systems – Proceedings of the Workshop (Astronomia); World Scientific Publishing Company (17 August 2007), {{ISBN|978-9812707055}}
* Plasmas in the Laboratory and in the Universe: New Insights and New Challenges (AIP Conference Proceedings); American Institute of Physics; 2004th edition (26 March 2004), {{ISBN|978-0735401761}}
